title: What did the server send?
fullTitle: The Browser Shows Your Page. What Does the Server Send?

scenes.narration: Two pages. Same article, headings, links and title. In a browser you cannot tell them apart. The server sent them very differently.
captions: Two pages. Same article, headings, links, title.
In a browser you cannot tell them apart.

scenes.narration: Fetch the raw HTML, before any script runs. The generated page carries the whole article: one h one, four h twos, six paragraphs, three links. The client-rendered page carries a shell: a loading line and one script tag. Zero article words of one hundred and ninety-eight. Same title and description on both.
captions: Raw HTML, before any script runs.
Generated page: 1 h1, 4 h2, 6 paragraphs, 3 links.
Client-rendered page: a shell and one script tag. 0 of 198 article words.

scenes.narration: The shell is not broken. Its script fetches article dot json and inserts the article. In a headless browser with JavaScript on, the client-rendered DOM ends with the same six paragraphs and three links. The article exists, but only in the browser's result.
captions: The script fetches /article.json and inserts the article.
With JavaScript on, both DOMs end with 6 paragraphs and 3 links.

scenes.narration: Disable JavaScript in a clean context. The generated page still shows the full article. The client-rendered page stays at Loading. Careful: a browser with scripts off is not a Googlebot simulator. Google can execute JavaScript. This only shows what each response contains on its own.
captions: JavaScript off: generated page still shows the article.
A browser with scripts off is not a Googlebot simulator. Google can run JS.

scenes.narration: Look again at the generated response. Text, headings and href attributes are already in the bytes the server sent. No script puts them there, and no hydration either: this article has no client interactivity.
captions: Generated response: text, headings and hrefs are already in the bytes.
No script, no hydration: the article has no client interactivity.

scenes.narration: Separate four things a search engine does. Crawl fetches. Render may execute scripts. Index decides what to store. Rank decides what to show. This test touches crawl and a slice of render. Static HTML guarantees neither indexing nor rankings, and server-rendered pages can still be rendered.
captions: Crawl fetches. Render may run scripts. Index stores. Rank shows.
This test touches crawl and a slice of render; nothing more.
Static HTML guarantees neither indexing nor rankings.

scenes.narration: Initial HTML and the eventual DOM are different artefacts. Inspect both, and know which you are looking at.
captions: Initial HTML and the eventual DOM are different artifacts.
Inspect both, and know which one you are looking at.
